title: Why remote work is dying and nobody wants to admit it

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Remote work is dying because it breaks collaboration, delays decision-making, and ignores human needs — all in the name of flexibility.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Flexibility isn't dying — it's evolving. Tools like Slack, Zoom, and GitHub let teams stay connected without being in the same room.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: But those tools can't replace in-person brainstorming. 53% of managers say remote teams struggle with innovation and trust.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Innovation thrives when people have autonomy. Distributed teams use async workflows and asynchronous communication to be more productive.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Remote work isn’t dying — it’s adapting. The future is hybrid, not rigid office hours or outdated protocols.
